title: XLOOKUP: find a matching value
goal: Look up a price, a name or any detail from a list with XLOOKUP, bring back the column you want, and fill the formula down safely with $ locks.

steps.text:
A customer says **“Samosa”**. What does it cost?

You could scroll down the menu and read across. With 6 items that's fine. With 600 items it's slow, and one slip gives the wrong price.

**XLOOKUP** does the hunt for you. You tell it three things:
• what to look for (`D2`)
• where to look (the item names)
• what to bring back (the prices)

Press **Play** to watch it built. XLOOKUP is in Microsoft 365 and Excel 2021 or newer.

frames.label: Click the cell for the answer
What to look for: click D2
Where to look: the item names
What to bring back: the prices

steps.prompt:
Every XLOOKUP needs two columns. First, the one Excel **searches**: the item names.

Press on ==A2== and drag down to ==A7==, then press [[Enter]].
steps.wrongFeedback: Select the six item names only: from **Tea** (`A2`) down to **Juice** (`A7`). Leave out the header and the prices.
clues: The Name Box shows `6R x 1C` when you have the right block.

steps.prompt:
Second, the column Excel **brings back** from: the prices.

Press on ==B2== and drag down to ==B7==, then press [[Enter]].
steps.wrongFeedback: Select the six prices, `B2` to `B7`. They must line up with the names row by row.
clues: Same six rows as the names, but one column to the right.

steps.prompt:
A customer ordered a **Samosa** (==D2==). Click ==E2== and type `=XLOOKUP(D2,A2:A7,B2:B7)`, then press [[Enter]].

Read it out loud: look for `D2` in `A2:A7`, and bring back the matching cell from `B2:B7`.
steps.explain: **15.** Excel found Samosa in the third row of the names, then brought back the third price. Change `D2` to **Cake** and the answer changes by itself.

wrongFeedback.missingFunction: Start with `=XLOOKUP(` and give it three parts separated by commas.
wrongFeedback.wrongValue: You should get **15**. Part two is the names (`A2:A7`, where to look) and part three is the prices (`B2:B7`, what to bring back). Swapped them? Excel can't find “Samosa” among prices.

clues: Three parts, separated by commas: `D2`, then the names, then the prices.

steps.prompt:
A teacher knows a **roll number** (==E2==) and needs the **name**.

Notice the roll numbers are in column B, to the **right** of the names. In ==F2==, search the roll numbers and bring back the name.
steps.explain: **Tom.** XLOOKUP can bring back a column on either side of the one it searched. Older lookup formulas can't look left. You'll meet them in Topic 35.

wrongFeedback.missingFunction: Use **XLOOKUP**: what to find, where to look, what to bring back.
wrongFeedback.wrongValue: Search the **roll numbers** (`B2:B7`) and bring back the **names** (`A2:A7`). Which is which?

clues: Where to look: the roll numbers. What to bring back: the names.

steps.topic: Use the answer in a sum
steps.prompt: A customer orders **3 Brownies**. In ==F2==, work out the bill: look up the price of the item in `D2`, then multiply it by the quantity in `E2`.
steps.explain: **75** (25 × 3). An XLOOKUP gives back a plain value, so you can multiply it, add it or join it like any other cell.

wrongFeedback.parseError: Check the brackets and commas, then add `*E2` at the end.
wrongFeedback.missingFunction: The price must come from a lookup, not typed in: use **XLOOKUP** for it.
wrongFeedback.wrongValue: One Brownie costs 25. The bill is the price **times** the quantity in `E2`.

steps.prompt:
Four orders are waiting in `D2:D5`, and you'll copy the formula down them. So **lock the two lists** with `$` first.

In ==E2==, type `=XLOOKUP(D2,$A$2:$A$7,$B$2:$B$7)`. (Click inside each range and press [[F4]] to add the `$` signs, or just type them.)
steps.explain: **25** for the Folder. The `$` signs pin the lists in place. `D2` has none, so it will move down to `D3`, `D4`, `D5` when you copy.

wrongFeedback.parseError: Check the brackets, commas and `$` signs: `=XLOOKUP(D2,$A$2:$A$7,$B$2:$B$7)`.
wrongFeedback.missingFunction: Use **XLOOKUP** with the two locked lists.
wrongFeedback.wrongValue: The first order is a **Folder**: its price is 25. Check the lookup value is `D2` and the lists are the names and prices.

clues: Same formula as before, with `$` in front of every column letter and row number in the two ranges.

steps.prompt:
`E2` to `E5` are selected, with your formula in the top cell.

Press [[Ctrl]] + [[D]] to copy it down. Every row looks up its **own** order, while the `$` lists stay put.
clues: Hold Ctrl, then tap D once.

steps.prompt:
Imagine you had left the `$` signs out. Filled down, the lists slide down one row at a time, so `E3` would hold `=XLOOKUP(D3,A3:A8,B3:B8)`.

`D3` says **Pen**, and Pen sits in `A2`. What would `E3` show?
options: `#N/A`: Pen is above the slid-down list
steps.explain: The new list starts at row 3, so Pen (row 2) has fallen off the top. Next, see it for yourself.
wrongFeedback: Excel doesn't remember where the list used to start. It only searches the cells the formula names now.
Nothing in the formula points at the Notebook row.
clues: Which rows does `A3:A8` cover? Is row 2 in there?

steps.prompt: Prove it. In ==E3==, type the formula Excel would have written without locks: `=XLOOKUP(D3,A3:A8,B3:B8)`.
steps.explain: **#N/A** means “not available”: Excel searched `A3:A8`, and Pen isn't there. Always lock the lists with `$` before you copy a lookup down. (Whole columns like `A:A` avoid the problem too.)

wrongFeedback.wrongValue: Use the slid-down lists exactly: `A3:A8` and `B3:B8`. Pen isn't in those rows, so you'll see an error.

clues: Notice the lists start at row **3** now, not row 2.

steps.prompt:
The menu has **Samosa**, yet `E2` shows `#N/A`. The order cell says **Samosas**.

Why didn't XLOOKUP find it?
options: XLOOKUP only finds an exact match: “Samosas” isn't “Samosa”
XLOOKUP can't search for text, only numbers
The prices must be sorted first
steps.explain: XLOOKUP is **exact** unless you tell it otherwise. Capitals don't matter (“samosa” works), but an extra letter or a stray space does. Tip: **TRIM** removes stray spaces. The next lesson shows how to show a friendly message instead of `#N/A`.
wrongFeedback: It searches text and numbers equally. Look closely at the two spellings.
XLOOKUP doesn't need any sorting for an exact match.
clues: Compare the order cell letter by letter with the menu.

steps.prompt:
The shop owner asks: **how many Bowls are in stock?** The item name is in ==E2==.

Put the answer in ==F2==.
steps.explain: **9 Bowls.** You searched the names, and brought back the **Stock** column, not the price next to it. Choosing the right column to bring back is the whole skill.

wrongFeedback.missingFunction: Look the item up: what to find, where to look, what to bring back.
wrongFeedback.wrongValue: Bowl's price is 75, but the question asks about **stock**. Bring back the Stock column.

clues: Search the item names. Bring back the column that holds the stock.
